outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the one development that directly bears on positive density is Theophilus Agama's arXiv:2007.02697 ('Ulam numbers have zero density', first posted 1 July 2020, latest revision v12 on 10 March 2026), which claims natural density zero, and I found no referee report, journal acceptance, expert commentary or refutation of it, while the Erdős problem database still lists the problem as open (last update 31 August 2025) and the 2026 AI-assisted notes on the Fourier 'hidden signal' are conditional on positive upper density and do not decide the question.
problem_asks: Whether the set of Ulam numbers has positive density. Unpacked: (1) the Ulam numbers, meaning the sequence a1 = 1, a2 = 2, with each later term the least integer above the previous term that is uniquely a sum of two distinct earlier terms (the (1,2)-Ulam sequence, OEIS A002858); (2) a density notion, which the bullet does not name, so the reading used in the literature and the Wikipedia article is natural density, with upper or lower density a different question; (3) whether that density is strictly greater than zero. A 'no' answer is density zero, the value Ulam is said to have conjectured. Erdős problem 342, which contains the same density question as its third part, also asks whether infinitely many pairs (a, a+2) occur and whether differences are eventually periodic; this bullet asks neither.

events.what_happened: Stefan Steinerberger, 'A Hidden Signal in the Ulam sequence', arXiv:1507.00267 (math.CO). Reports numerically that a real alpha approximately 2.5714474995 makes the values alpha*a_n mod 2pi non-uniform (an absolutely continuous, non-uniform measure), with cos(alpha*a_n) < 0 for every term of the first 10^7 except 2, 3, 47 and 69; calls it an empirical 'global rigidity phenomenon'. The abstract page contains no statement about density.
events.revisions: v1 1 Jul 2015; v2 13 Sep 2015; v3 4 Oct 2015; v4 28 Nov 2015; v5 24 Feb 2016; v6 6 Jul 2016 (current). A Yale report (YALEU/DCS/TR-1508, May 2015) is said by a search snippet to carry the first version; not opened.
events.delivers: A numerical observation about the distribution of alpha*a_n mod 2pi, computed by machine. Nothing about the density of the Ulam numbers, positive or zero.
events.directly_checkable: The cosine sums can be recomputed from the first terms of the sequence; that is a finite check of a distributional observation, not of density.
events.direction: Does not bear on the direction of the density question.

events.what_happened: Joshua Hinman, Borys Kuca, Alexander Schlesinger and Arseniy Sheydvasser, 'The Unreasonable Rigidity of Ulam Sets', arXiv:1711.00145 (single version, 31 Oct 2017). The abstract says 'For Ulam sequences, using elementary methods we give an upper bound on the density' in the journal abstract, and 'an upper bound on the density of Ulam sequences U(1,n)' in the arXiv abstract. Published as 'Rigidity of Ulam sets and sequences', Involve 12(3) (2019), with received 10 Jul 2018 and accepted 5 Sep 2018 on the Involve page.
events.revisions: arXiv: v1 only (31 Oct 2017, 24 pages). Involve page gives published 14 Dec 2018 while the issue is labelled 2019; not reconciled.
events.delivers: An upper bound on the density of Ulam sequences U(1,n), a family that includes U(1,2) (the Ulam numbers), obtained by elementary methods. The numerical value of the bound and its proof were not read. An upper bound does not decide whether the density is positive.
events.remains: Whether the density of U(1,2) is positive; the bullet's question is untouched.

checked_by.qualification: peer-reviewed mathematics journal; referees are not named on the page
checked_by.what_they_did: accepted and published the paper in Involve 12(3)

events.direction: An upper density bound on U(1,n); cuts toward neither answer to the positivity question.

events.what_happened: Philip Gibbs and Judson McCranie, 'The Ulam Numbers up to One Trillion' (2017), a computation of the Ulam numbers to about 10^12 cited by Wikipedia; a search snippet of a later paper by Sheydvasser says it confirmed a periodicity conjecture for U(1,2) through the first trillion terms. The paper was not located, so this is second-hand.
events.delivers: Numerical data on the sequence to about 10^12 (second-hand). A computation, which cannot determine an asymptotic density.
events.directly_checkable: The sequence values can be recomputed from the definition; the computation itself was not checked.
events.direction: None; the data are consistent with a density near 0.074 at that range.

events.what_happened: Theophilus Agama, 'Ulam numbers have zero density', arXiv:2007.02697 (sole author, math.NT). Claims that the natural density of the Ulam numbers is zero, that is, that the count of Ulam numbers in [1,k] divided by k tends to 0 (Theorem 5.1). As read from the v12 HTML: Prop 4.4 embeds finite Ulam prefixes in addition chains; Prop 3.6 gives a lower bound C(n) >> n/log2(n) for a chain quantity C(n), resting on Lemma 3.4, whose bounds are cited to Schonhage and Brauer and not proved (Remark 3.5 says the implicit constant is 'by no means easy' to find, so only a lower bound is used). A second route in Section 6, the 'circle of partition' (CoP), gives density zero only under an extra hypothesis (Theorem 6.8).
events.revisions: v1 1 Jul 2020 (abstract page comment: 6 pages); v2 7 Jul 2020; v3 24 Nov 2020; v4 18 Jan 2021; v5 20 Jan 2021; v6 22 Jan 2021; v7 25 Jan 2021; v8 21 Apr 2021; v9 11 Oct 2021; v10 9 Jul 2023; v11 27 Aug 2023; v12 10 Mar 2026 (inside the window; 11 pages; comment: 'reformatted and introduction expanded; ideas remain unchanged'). The v1 PDF's structure lists Sections 1 to 5 and References with no Section 6, so the CoP route was added in some later version; I could not establish which, since the v1 body text was unreadable. The abstract page gives no per-version change notes. Versions v2 to v11 were not opened.
events.delivers: If the Section 5 argument holds: the natural density of the Ulam numbers is zero (Theorem 5.1, stated without explicit hypotheses), which answers the bullet's question negatively for natural density. Restrictions: natural density only; upper and lower density are not addressed in any version read. The Section 6 CoP route reaches the same conclusion only under its stated hypothesis, which the text, as read, assumes rather than verifies.
events.remains: If the Section 5 argument fails, the whole question. Upper and lower density are not addressed.
events.time_since_posted: 6 years 3 months since v1 (July 2020); 7 months since v12 (10 March 2026)
events.doubts: (1) Theorem 5.1 depends on Prop 3.6 and Lemma 3.4, whose bounds are cited to Schonhage and Brauer and not proved in the text. I did not check the lemma or the inequality chain. I could not reconcile C(n) with the single-integer addition-chain lower bounds I found (an unopened survey, arXiv:2504.07332, snippet gives l(n) >= log2 n + log2 nu(n) - 2.13 for one integer n), so the n/log n shape is unexplained by me. (2) The numerics point the other way at accessible sizes: OEIS A002858 reports density near 0.074 from calculations to 6.759 x 10^8 (McCranie), a(10^9) = 13517664323 (comment dated Aug 2015), a fit of the first 3 million terms to the line 13.51n (Sloane, 2006), and waves of period about 21.6 (Wilson; McCranie). A search snippet attributes a density of about 0.0739 from the first 11,172,261 terms (up to 150,999,995) to Strottman; not opened. Finite data cannot settle an asymptotic density, but the claim is in tension with the apparent trend, and neither the abstract nor the text I read reconciles them. (3) The Section 6 route is conditional on a hypothesis the text assumes, per the HTML reading. (4) The proof's architecture changed between versions: the v1 outline has no CoP section while the claim (density zero) is the same in v1. (5) The same author's CoP framework, applied to the Erdos-Turan additive base conjecture (arXiv:1707.05679), carries an arXiv comment that the paper 'had undergone peer review but not well understood by experts' and that 'a new remark has been added at the end of the proof to clarify certain misunderstanding of the reviewers' (v7, Feb 2024). The earlier Erdos-Turan preprint (arXiv:2010.11857, v3 Mar 2026) says only that it 'formulate[s] and prove[s] several variants' of the conjecture. (6) I found no journal record, zbMATH or MathSciNet entry (not reachable from my tools), expert review, blog post, citing paper or refutation. The Erdos problem 342 database entry still shows the problem open, last updated 31 August 2025, and the Wikipedia lead (last edited 7 Sep 2026) says the density 'seem[s] to' be about 0.07398 and does not mention the claim.
events.direction: Points to the answer 'no' for natural density (density zero), the value Wikipedia and OEIS attribute to Ulam's conjecture, and against the numerical picture of density about 0.074.

events.what_happened: Paul Adutwum, Hopper Clark, Ro Emerson, Alexandra Sheydvasser, Arseniy Sheydvasser and Axelle Tougouma, 'Distributions of Ulam Words up to Length 30', arXiv:2410.01217. The object is Ulam words, after Bade, Cui, Labelle and Li, not the Ulam numbers. The abstract gives lower bounds on how many Ulam words there are of each length, reports structure in gaps and special words, and sharpens conjectures of Bade et al. The abstract states no density conjecture. A search snippet says the work appeared in Integers in 2025 and conjectures a density exponent for Ulam words; not verified.
events.delivers: Counts and structure of Ulam words up to length 30. A different object, so nothing about the density of the Ulam numbers.
events.direction: None on the bullet's direction; a neighbouring object.

events.what_happened: Francois Clement and Stefan Steinerberger, 'Small gaps in the Ulam sequence', arXiv:2501.16285, published in Comptes Rendus Mathematique 363 (2025), pp. 941-949, DOI 10.5802/crmath.746. The abstract page says the paper improves the best upper bound on the growth of the sequence and shows that some small gaps must exist: for some c > 0 and all n, the minimum over 1 <= k <= n of a(k+1)/a(k) is at most 1 + c log(n)/n. A forum post of 21 Jan 2026 refers to a constant 1.454 in the paper's Theorem 1; not verified from the full text.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only (27 Jan 2025). Journal page: received 30 Jan 2025, accepted 29 Mar 2025, published 5 Sep 2025.
events.delivers: An improved growth upper bound and a small-ratio result for consecutive terms. Neither concerns density.
events.remains: The whole density question; the abstract and journal pages do not discuss density.

checked_by.what_they_did: accepted the paper (29 Mar 2025) and published it (5 Sep 2025)

events.direction: None on the bullet's direction; growth and gap quantities, not density.

events.what_happened: Frank Gilson, 'Arithmetical Complexity and Absoluteness of Rigidity Phenomena for Ulam Sequences', arXiv:2511.13066 (math.LO). The abstract, as read: membership in U(a,b) and its increasing enumeration are uniformly primitive recursive; a family-level finite-window rigidity statement has a Pi^0_3 upper bound; for an individual U(a,b), eventual periodicity of gaps and finiteness of residue classes are Sigma^0_2; rational upper-density, lower-density and exact-density assertions have Pi^0_3 upper bounds, which the abstract calls 'classifications by upper bounds, not completeness claims'.
events.revisions: v1 17 Nov 2025; v2 2 Dec 2025; v3 10 Sep 2026 (current), commented 'Major correction'. Per the abstract-page comment, v3 replaces the fixed-pair claims and several complexity and absoluteness claims and removes unsupported completeness, reverse-mathematics and model-theory overclaims.
events.delivers: Logical-complexity classifications of density statements for the family U(a,b), which includes U(1,2). It determines no density value and no positivity; the abstract disclaims completeness claims.
events.doubts: The v3 'Major correction' concedes that earlier complexity, absoluteness and completeness claims were overstated. It is recorded as a correction, not a withdrawal of the main classification.
events.direction: None on the bullet's direction; a logic classification of density statements.

events.what_happened: Przemek Chojecki, Erdos Problems forum thread 342, post of 20 Jan 2026 16:12: 'I managed to get an explanation with GPT-5.2 of why a hidden signal might arise', linking a write-up at https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos342.pdf and adding 'This is conjectural but fits the quasi-periodic picture.' The PDF could not be read (WebFetch returned compressed PDF bytes). Forum summaries describe a conditional argument: if U(1,2) has positive upper density, the Fourier spike is not a fluke. The Erdos AI-contributions tracker (teorth/erdosproblems wiki, section 1(d), 'AI collaborating with humans') lists the entry with humans 'Przemek Chojecki', AI 'GPT-5.2 Pro, GPT-5.4 Pro', dates '20 Jan-23 Mar, 2026' and outcome 'Partial result'.
events.revisions: A later note by the same poster is dated 23 Mar 2026 (next event). The 20 Jan PDF has no revision history visible.
events.delivers: Per the forum post's description (write-up unread): a conjectural explanation of the numerical Fourier signal in the Ulam sequence, conditional on positive upper density of U(1,2). It establishes no positivity and no density value.
events.remains: Positivity of the density, natural or upper: nothing established. The explanation itself remains conjectural by its author's own description.

checked_by.what_they_did: ran a ChatGPT check which 'flagged some issues with the writeup' (20 Jan 2026 16:30), and suggested asking ChatGPT to check its own work; the poster replied that their ChatGPT agreed with the critique (17:00) and that self-checks eventually stop finding anything (19:32)

events.doubts: The author calls the explanation conjectural. An AI check flagged issues with the first write-up, and the poster agreed that the critique held and that the write-up needed reworking (per forum summaries). The only checks reported are AI checks, not human readings. The thread's page counters show 0 proof claims and 0 proof expositions.
events.direction: Neither proves nor disproves positivity; it is conditional on the positive-density side of the question, so it cuts toward the 'yes' answer only as an assumption.

events.what_happened: Przemek Chojecki, Erdos forum thread 342, post of 23 Mar 2026 10:40: 'After a longer back and forth with GPT-5.4 I've got some new partial results in the direction I wanted', linking https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos342-new.pdf with the words 'Here's the note that proves the following'. The PDF could not be read (compressed PDF bytes). Forum text and a search snippet quoting the thread describe the note as conditional: if the classical Ulam sequence U(1,2) has positive upper density, then the Fourier spike people see numerically is not a fluke. The argument passes to a limiting dynamical system, and its finite input is that the initial segments contain at most 3|A_N| ordered Schur triples x+y=z, from which Green's theorem places A_N close to a sum-free set. The tracker lists it in the same 1(d) row as the 20 Jan note.
events.delivers: Per the forum description (note unread): a conditional argument that, assuming positive upper density of U(1,2), the Fourier spike is structural. It does not establish positive density; the assumption it uses is the 'yes' answer to the question itself.
events.remains: Positive density, natural or upper: not established. The note's conditional does not discharge the hypothesis.

disputes.summary: Who conjectured density zero. OEIS A002858 says 'Ulam conjectured that this sequence has density 0'. Wikipedia's footnotes say Ulam's 1964a paper does not address density, his 1964b paper poses the density question without conjecturing a value, and Recaman (1973) likewise poses it without a value. The Erdos problem 342 page credits the problem to Ulam. Not resolved here.

summary: The search (41 web queries, listed below) and the sources opened found one development that bears directly on the density question: Theophilus Agama's arXiv:2007.02697, 'Ulam numbers have zero density', first posted 1 July 2020 and revised to v12 on 10 March 2026. Its Theorem 5.1 claims natural density zero with no explicit hypotheses. I read the v12 HTML and the v1 abstract page; the v1 PDF body could not be read, and v2 to v11 were not opened. The Section 5 argument rests on Prop 3.6 and Lemma 3.4, whose bounds are cited to Schonhage and Brauer rather than proved, and the Section 6 'circle of partition' route is conditional on a counting hypothesis the text assumes. I did not check the lemmas against the full text. I found no referee report, journal acceptance, expert commentary, citing paper, or refutation, and I could not query zbMATH or MathSciNet with my tools. The Erdos problem 342 database entry still shows the problem open, last updated 31 August 2025, and it records the formal statement as 'formalized: yes' (2026-03-17) while the same entry says 'formal_status: unformalized'. The formal-conjectures Lean file states the three open parts with sorry, and the proven test lemmas do not touch density. Wikipedia's lead (last edited 7 September 2026) presents the density as an empirical figure of about 0.07398 and does not mention the claim. Numerics (OEIS, with McCranie's data to 6.759 x 10^8 and a(10^9) = 13517664323, Sloane's line fit 13.51n, and a density of about 0.0739 from a computation to about 1.5 x 10^8 attributed to Strottman by a search snippet) are consistent with positive density at accessible sizes; finite data cannot settle an asymptotic question. The author's same CoP framework, applied to the Erdos-Turan additive base conjecture (arXiv:1707.05679), carries an arXiv comment that experts 'not well understood' it, and the author's 2010 Erdos-Turan preprint claims only variants. Earlier results: Hinman, Kuca, Schlesinger and Sheydvasser (2017; Involve 2019) give an upper density bound for U(1,n), value unread, which does not decide positivity; Steinerberger (2015) and Gibbs and McCranie (2017) are numerical. Clement and Steinerberger (2025, Comptes Rendus 2025) and Gilson (2025; v3 'Major correction' 2026) do not decide the density. On AI: no system is named in any source on Agama's claim, and the v12 text contains no AI or assistance statement. AI involvement appears only in the 2026 Erdos 342 forum thread. Chojecki's notes of 20 Jan 2026 (credited to GPT-5.2) and 23 Mar 2026 (credited to GPT-5.4) give conditional results on the Fourier 'hidden signal', assuming positive upper density; neither PDF could be read, so their content rests on forum text and search snippets. The teorth AI-contributions tracker lists the entry as 'AI collaborating with humans', 'Partial result', naming 'GPT-5.2 Pro, GPT-5.4 Pro' (tracker tier names, not the authors' wording). MalekZ's 23 Mar posts name GPT-5.4 and state no result. AlphaProof Nexus's attempted list includes erdos_342.parts.i to iii, with no visible result; the repository's per-problem listings are partial. Ulam words (2024) and the Ulam-word density question are a different object. Close calls: (a) whether the Section 5 argument, if accepted, is a density-zero proof, which needs a specialist's reading of Prop 3.6 and Lemma 3.4, and whether the Section 6 route adds anything; (b) whether the 2026 notes count as AI-load-bearing: the poster credits GPT with the explanation and with the partial results, which is their own account, but the notes are conditional and address the hidden-signal question rather than density; (c) whether the conditional on positive upper density is a different question from the bullet's natural-density question. ulam.ai, which hosts the notes, describes itself on its homepage as a company that builds reasoning datasets and benchmarks for AI labs; its research list of 28 items has no entry for problem 342, and the link between that company and the poster is not established in any source I opened.
competing_reading: Read Agama's arXiv:2007.02697 as a resolution. Theorem 5.1 states natural density zero without explicit hypotheses and rests on a lower bound that is classical in form; the finite-range numerics (about 0.074 to 6.8 x 10^8, and the first 3 million terms fitting 13.51n) describe accessible sizes and cannot decide an asymptotic density, so the claim is not refuted by data. On that reading the bullet is answered negatively for natural density, with the caveat that the answer is unrefereed after six years and that upper and lower density are untouched. The opposing reading: the proof has no journal record or expert engagement; its key lemma is cited, not proved; its Section 6 route is conditional; its architecture changed between versions while the claim did not; the same author's CoP framework has a comment that reviewers did not understand it; and the numerics show a stable density near 0.074 over the range computed. On that reading the question stays open and the claim should be treated as unverified.
what_would_settle_it: (a) A referee report, journal acceptance, or a specialist's written verification or refutation of Section 5, in particular Prop 3.6 and Lemma 3.4 of arXiv:2007.02697, and of the hypothesis of the Section 6 route. (b) A published correction or error identified in those steps. (c) A proof of density zero or positive density, since no finite computation can settle the asymptotic question. (d) For the AI half: the 20 Jan and 23 Mar 2026 PDFs read in full (erdos342.pdf and erdos342-new.pdf), whether the Section 6 CoP material was added in v12 or earlier (reading v2 to v11), and the per-problem result list of AlphaProof Nexus for erdos_342.parts.i to iii (the ErdosProblems folder listing is partial).
